name: The staircase of horror
hint: The everyday cracks, step by step, until nothing is safe and the fear shows what it is really about.

parts.title: The everyday
chapters: The place and the people
(ca 5 %) Show ordinary life, what the main character wants and stands to lose, and their private fear, with a first omen on page one.
The first strange thing
(ca 10 %) A small thing that does not add up and can be explained away: the reader should sense more than the main character does.
The explanations
(ca 15 %) Everyone, the main character included, finds a reasonable explanation. A reason to stay makes leaving hard.

parts.title: It grows
chapters: The pattern
(ca 25 %) The events repeat and follow something like rules. Show one rule in action without explaining it.
Closer
(ca 35 %) The threat gets into what ought to be safe: the home, the bed, the body or someone close.
No one believes
(ca 42 %) The main character asks for help and is dismissed. Being alone becomes a threat in itself.
The first price
(ca 50 %) Someone is hurt, vanishes or dies. From now on the reader knows that anyone can be next.

parts.title: The truth
chapters: The false calm
(ca 58 %) After the loss it seems possible to live with. Grief, closeness and a plan give the reader room to breathe, which is exactly why the next step hits harder.
What happened here
(ca 65 %) The main character learns where the threat comes from and what it wants. The truth should make things worse, not easier.
The escape that fails
(ca 75 %) An attempt to get away or stop the threat goes wrong and reveals a rule nobody knew.
Cut off
(ca 80 %) The ways out close: the car, the phone, the friends. The main character faces their private fear head on.

parts.title: The worst
chapters: The descent
(ca 85 %) The main character chooses to go where they least want to, the cellar, the woods or the memory, because it is the only way.
The confrontation
(ca 92 %) The threat is met on its own terms, and the rules set up earlier decide the outcome, not luck.
The echo
(ca 98 %) What survived and what did not. Leave one last unease that follows the reader out of the book.
